# CallCatcher Xposed module/apk for recording, organizing and playing phone and WhatsApp calls. ## What motivated me to create CC: There are already excellent tools like BCR and WAE, but having to configure a folder for saving files, dealing with a file manager, or running into SAF (Storage Access Framework) restrictions when trying to save files to other apps can become quite annoying. So, I created a single app that: - Requires no configuration (other than installing the module and APK, and granting the necessary permissions via Vector/LSPosed) - Automatically categorizes recordings by type and color - Includes a built-in player - Has no notification system (it’s unnecessary) ## Preview Note: The display of "Whatsapp Contact" is intentional and serves only as a preview; the CC field displays the name correctly.
## How it works One shared capture engine (`AudioRecord` → MediaCodec Opus → Ogg) runs in the CallCatcher app process. Triggers only say _when_ a call starts and ends: | Trigger | Where it runs | Signal | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Phone calls | `PhoneCallRecordingService` (InCallService) in the app | Telecom call state | | WhatsApp calls (Telecom) | same InCallService, if WhatsApp registers its calls with Telecom | Telecom call state | | WhatsApp calls (hook) | `:capture-wa` inside WhatsApp, via LSPosed/Vector | `soundPortCreated` / `fieldstatsReady`, sent to the app's `TriggerProvider` | | Recording | microphone recording (voice memo) from the bottom dock, until Stop | button | Capture needs `CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT` and call-state access needs `CONTROL_INCALL_EXPERIENCE`. Both are **privileged permissions**: `pm grant` cannot grant them, which is why WAEnhancer (recording from inside WhatsApp) falls back to the microphone. Like BCR, CallCatcher gets them by being installed as a **privileged system app** through a KernelSU/Magisk module. ### Capture profiles - **Phone:** `VOICE_CALL` → `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` → `MIC`. `VOICE_CALL` is confirmed on the target device (Redmi Note 12, BCR logs): both sides, 16 kHz mono. The network sets the quality ceiling, so Opus at 16 kHz / 32 kbps is transparent. - **WhatsApp:** first test (MIC only, 48 kHz) showed why WAE sounds bad: the other party is not in any microphone source, and `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` is silenced for other apps while WhatsApp uses it. So the VoIP profile is: 1. `VOICE_CALL`, skipped automatically if digitally silent during the 1.5 s start window; 2. **two-leg**: your side from `MIC`, the other side from playback capture of voice-communication audio (`PlaybackCapture`: loop-back audio policy, needs `MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING` + `CAPTURE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION_OUTPUT`), each auto-levelled, mixed to mono; 3. `MIC` alone as the last resort. The details line of a recording shows which one won (`MIC+PLAYBACK` is the target), and "Last saved" in the setup card lists why earlier ones were skipped. Test with BCR and WAEnhancer's call recording **disabled**: they open the same audio sources at the same time. ## Install (test builds) CI (`.github/workflows/android.yml`) builds on every push and uploads one artifact with: - `CallCatcher-.apk`: the app, which is also the LSPosed module; - `CallCatcher-module-.zip`: KernelSU/Magisk module that installs that APK in `/system/priv-app` with its permission allowlist. Requirement: the root solution must be able to mount module files into `/system`. - **Magisk**: built in, nothing to add. - **KernelSU**: recent versions no longer mount module files themselves; install a **metamodule** first (as for BCR). After reboot, the metamodule should list CallCatcher as mounted. First install: 1. Uninstall any CallCatcher installed as a normal app with a different signing key. 2. Flash the module zip in KernelSU and reboot. (If the phone doesn't boot, KernelSU's safe mode, volume-down during boot, disables modules.) 3. Open CallCatcher, accept the notice and the permissions. The status panel should show all checks green. 4. In Vector, enable the CallCatcher module with scope **WhatsApp** and **System Framework**, then reboot. System Framework is needed so WhatsApp can reach the app (Android 11+ package visibility). Later builds with the same permissions: install the new APK over the old one; no reflash needed. If the permissions change, reflash the module. ### Signing Updates only install if every APK has the same signature. CI signs with the key in the `DEV_KEYSTORE_B64` repository secret (base64 of `ui/dev.keystore`, which is git-ignored). Without the secret, CI warns and uses a throwaway key. ## Testing checklist - "Recording" (bottom dock), then "Stop": the recording appears under Today; tap it to open the player deck (play, speed, share, delete, close), tap or drag the waveform to seek. - Phone call: the deck's details line should read `VOICE_CALL`. - WhatsApp call: the setup card (status pill, top right) shows "WhatsApp trigger: last …" if the hook reached the app; the deck shows which strategy won. Hook diagnostics are in Vector → Logs, lines starting with `CallCatcher:`. - Share: share button in the deck opens the system share sheet (e.g. send to a WhatsApp chat). - Delete: trash button in the deck, tap twice. ## Modules | Module | Role | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `:core` | Capture engine, storage, Room DB, Opus encoding, RecorderService, TriggerProvider. | | `:capture-phone` | InCallService trigger and foreground host (BCR model). | | `:capture-wa` | LSPosed hooks: WhatsApp call detection, package-visibility fix in system_server. WhatsApp class lookup is isolated in `WaClassFinder`. | | `:player` | Media3/ExoPlayer playback wrapper. | | `:ui` | Total-black app: one filterable list, status panel, player. | ## License CallCatcher is free software, licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE). You can redistribute and modify it under those terms; it comes with no warranty. ## Legal Recording your own conversations is generally lawful, but rules vary by country and by use. The app shows a first-run notice to that effect and disclaims responsibility for how recordings are used.
readmeHTML:
CallCatcher

Xposed module/apk for recording, organizing and playing phone and WhatsApp calls.

What motivated me to create CC:

There are already excellent tools like BCR and WAE, but having to configure a folder for saving files, dealing with a file manager, or running into SAF (Storage Access Framework) restrictions when trying to save files to other apps can become quite annoying.

So, I created a single app that:

  • Requires no configuration (other than installing the module and APK, and granting the necessary permissions via Vector/LSPosed)
  • Automatically categorizes recordings by type and color
  • Includes a built-in player
  • Has no notification system (it’s unnecessary)

    • Preview

    Note: The display of "Whatsapp Contact" is intentional and serves only as a preview; the CC field displays the name correctly.


    How it works

    One shared capture engine (AudioRecord → MediaCodec Opus → Ogg) runs in the CallCatcher app

    process. Triggers only say _when_ a call starts and ends:

    | Trigger | Where it runs | Signal |

    | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

    | Phone calls | PhoneCallRecordingService (InCallService) in the app | Telecom call state |

    | WhatsApp calls (Telecom) | same InCallService, if WhatsApp registers its calls with Telecom | Telecom call state |

    | WhatsApp calls (hook) | :capture-wa inside WhatsApp, via LSPosed/Vector | soundPortCreated / fieldstatsReady, sent to the app's TriggerProvider |

    | Recording | microphone recording (voice memo) from the bottom dock, until Stop | button |

    Capture needs CAPTURE_AUDIO_OUTPUT and call-state access needs CONTROL_INCALL_EXPERIENCE. Both

    are privileged permissions: pm grant cannot grant them, which is why WAEnhancer (recording from

    inside WhatsApp) falls back to the microphone. Like BCR, CallCatcher gets them by being installed as

    a privileged system app through a KernelSU/Magisk module.

    Capture profiles

  • **Phone:** `VOICE_CALL` → `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` → `MIC`. `VOICE_CALL` is confirmed on the target

    • device (Redmi Note 12, BCR logs): both sides, 16 kHz mono. The network sets the quality ceiling,

    so Opus at 16 kHz / 32 kbps is transparent.

  • **WhatsApp:** first test (MIC only, 48 kHz) showed why WAE sounds bad: the other party is not in

    • any microphone source, and VOICE_COMMUNICATION is silenced for other apps while WhatsApp uses

    it. So the VoIP profile is:

    1. VOICE_CALL, skipped automatically if digitally silent during the 1.5 s start window;

    2. two-leg: your side from MIC, the other side from playback capture of

    voice-communication audio (PlaybackCapture: loop-back audio policy, needs

    MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING + CAPTURE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION_OUTPUT), each auto-levelled, mixed to mono;

    3. MIC alone as the last resort.

    The details line of a recording shows which one won (MIC+PLAYBACK is the target), and

    "Last saved" in the setup card lists why earlier ones were skipped.

    Test with BCR and WAEnhancer's call recording disabled: they open the same audio sources at the

    same time.

    Install (test builds)

    CI (.github/workflows/android.yml) builds on every push and uploads one artifact with:

  • `CallCatcher-.apk`: the app, which is also the LSPosed module;
  • `CallCatcher-module-.zip`: KernelSU/Magisk module that installs that APK in

    • /system/priv-app with its permission allowlist.

    Requirement: the root solution must be able to mount module files into /system.

  • **Magisk**: built in, nothing to add.
  • **KernelSU**: recent versions no longer mount module files themselves; install a **metamodule**

    • first (as for BCR). After reboot, the metamodule should list CallCatcher as mounted.

    First install:

  • Uninstall any CallCatcher installed as a normal app with a different signing key.
  • Flash the module zip in KernelSU and reboot. (If the phone doesn't boot, KernelSU's safe mode,

    • volume-down during boot, disables modules.)

  • Open CallCatcher, accept the notice and the permissions. The status panel should show all

    • checks green.

  • In Vector, enable the CallCatcher module with scope **WhatsApp** and **System Framework**, then

    • reboot. System Framework is needed so WhatsApp can reach the app (Android 11+ package visibility).

    Later builds with the same permissions: install the new APK over the old one; no reflash needed.

    If the permissions change, reflash the module.

    Signing

    Updates only install if every APK has the same signature. CI signs with the key in the

    DEV_KEYSTORE_B64 repository secret (base64 of ui/dev.keystore, which is git-ignored). Without the

    secret, CI warns and uses a throwaway key.

    Testing checklist

  • "Recording" (bottom dock), then "Stop": the recording appears under Today; tap it to open the

    • player deck (play, speed, share, delete, close), tap or drag the waveform to seek.

  • Phone call: the deck's details line should read `VOICE_CALL`.
  • WhatsApp call: the setup card (status pill, top right) shows "WhatsApp trigger: last …" if the

    • hook reached the app; the deck shows which strategy won. Hook diagnostics are in Vector → Logs,

    lines starting with CallCatcher:.

  • Share: share button in the deck opens the system share sheet (e.g. send to a WhatsApp chat).
  • Delete: trash button in the deck, tap twice.

    • Modules

    | Module | Role |

    | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

    | :core | Capture engine, storage, Room DB, Opus encoding, RecorderService, TriggerProvider. |

    | :capture-phone | InCallService trigger and foreground host (BCR model). |

    | :capture-wa | LSPosed hooks: WhatsApp call detection, package-visibility fix in system_server. WhatsApp class lookup is isolated in WaClassFinder. |

    | :player | Media3/ExoPlayer playback wrapper. |

    | :ui | Total-black app: one filterable list, status panel, player. |

    License

    CallCatcher is free software, licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

    You can redistribute and modify it under those terms; it comes with no warranty.

    Legal

    Recording your own conversations is generally lawful, but rules vary by country and by use. The app

    shows a first-run notice to that effect and disclaims responsibility for how recordings are used.
